page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.medium is an entry-level memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and custom AWS Graviton ARMv9 architecture. The instance features a single dedicated physical Neoverse-V2 core operating at 2.8 GHz, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. The underlying processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptographic instructions. No discrete GPUs are attached, but the configuration bundles a dedicated 59 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume alongside a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluation highlights the architectural characteristics of a single high-efficiency ARM core. Single-threaded metrics are consistent with general ARMv9 capabilities, posting a Geekbench single-core score of 1741.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1694.58. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression exhibits strong throughput at 14.0 GB/sec, while single-threaded gzip compression operates at 30.04 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks and aggregate metrics across the suite place the instance in the lower percentiles due strictly to the single-vCPU ceiling. Memory bandwidth delivers 30.06 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 11.68 GB/sec on writes, supporting 2.45 million Redis SET operations per second.

Cost efficiency is driven by the density of memory and high-speed local NVMe storage relative to the minimal compute footprint. Organizations requiring moderate working memory with low-latency ephemeral disk access can avoid over-provisioning compute cores. However, overall performance is strictly bounded by single-thread capability, making the instance ill-suited for parallelized compute tasks. AWS r8gd.medium is technically optimized for lightweight in-memory caching nodes, small Redis or Memcached instances, staging environments, ephemeral batch preprocessing, and microservices requiring fast local disk scratch space.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gd.medium is a memory-optimized cloud instance driven by AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is provisioned with 1 dedicated physical core at 2.8 GHz, 8.0 GB of memory, and 59 GB of bundled high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, supported by a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results reflect standard single-core execution with average single-threaded CPU scores, strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 14.0 GB/sec, and an overall throughput envelope capped by the single available vCPU. With an 8:1 memory-to-CPU ratio and low-latency ephemeral storage, the hardware configuration targets workloads requiring high memory allocation per core without excessive compute overhead. It is well-matched for lightweight caching, Redis, staging datastores, ephemeral data handling, and lightweight web or microservice deployments.
